subject: POC Trial Planning & Workload Intake — SaaSify / Redwood
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@saasify.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T15:12:00Z
Subject: POC Trial Planning — Recap & workload intake

Hi Elaine — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we start provisioning the trial environment.

Recap (from our discovery)
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Inference for in-app recommendations and multi-turn prompts in SaaSify’s editor product.
- Primary success criteria (customer): maintain UI quality while keeping cost predictable; concrete KPIs below.
- Timeline target: 2-3 week evaluation window, ideally starting in the week of Jun 29.

Required from SaaSify (workload & traffic intake) — please confirm and fill in any numbers we missed:
- Average steady-state RPS: ______
- Expected peak RPS (sustained spikes): ______
- Burst spikes (short bursts and duration): ______
- Typical concurrency (simultaneous active requests): ______
- Avg prompt token length (user prompt + history): ______
- Avg completion tokens (model output): ______
- % of requests with long context (>1024 tokens): ______
- Test dataset: will you provide a representative replay / sample file?

Proposed POC plan (high-level)
1) Kickoff & access (day 0): create service account, share sample traffic, sign trial terms (attached). (Owner: Ben / SaaSify ops)
2) Provisioning (day 1-3): Redwood provisions trial capacity and warms caches; run smoke tests. (Owner: Marissa)
3) Workload replay & tuning (week 1): run replay, adjust batching/quant profiles, collect perf/quality metrics. (Owner: Marissa / Dylan)
4) Validation & QA (week 2): run keystone prompt set, measure quality regressions, iterate prompts. (Owner: Elaine / Tom)
5) Wrap & next steps (end of trial): review metrics, discuss Dedicated/Private options and procurement. (Owner: Ben / SaaSify procurement)

Suggested success criteria (to agree):
- Latency: p95 generation time < 300 ms for interactive flows OR < 400 ms for multi-turn recommendation flows.
- Throughput: system sustains expected steady-state RPS with safety margin + handles peak bursts (see numbers above).
- Quality: keystone prompt pass-rate >= 90% (customer-defined rubric) and no critical hallucinations on core intents.
- Reliability: > 99% successful responses (no errors/timeouts) during test window.
- Cost target: runway estimate within the budget SaaSify shared during call.

Attachments: saasify-poc-plan.xlsx (POC template), redwood-trial-terms.pdf (trial T&Cs).

Next steps / asks:
- Elaine: please confirm the workload numbers above and share a 1-2 day sample replay if possible.
- If numbers look right, we’ll schedule a 30 min kickoff with Marissa and Dylan to walk through access and replay format (proposed dates below).

Proposed kickoff slots: Thu Jun 25 10:00-10:30 PT, Fri Jun 26 09:00-09:30 PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0199
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@saasify.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@saasify.com>, procurement@saasify.com
Date: 2026-06-19T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: POC Trial Planning — Recap & workload intake

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear plan. Below are the initial workload numbers from our platform team (Tom included). We’ll also upload a 48-hour sample replay (anonymized) to the Drive link you shared by EOD Monday.

SaaSify workload profile (current estimates)
- Average steady-state RPS: 18 requests/sec (approx 1,080 requests/min)
- Expected high sustained peak: 120 RPS for 8-12 minutes (midday load)
- Burst spikes: up to 240 RPS for short bursts (~1-3 minutes) during campaign launches
- Typical concurrency: 35 concurrent active model calls
- Avg prompt tokens: 75 tokens (includes minimal history)
- Avg completion tokens: 210 tokens
- % requests with long context (>1024 tokens): ~9% (historical chat sessions + doc contexts)
- Estimated test duration: 3 weeks (we prefer a slightly longer window to exercise weekly campaign patterns)

Success criteria clarifications:
- Latency target: p95 < 400 ms for recommendation API (we can be stricter for interactive editor flows)
- Quality: intent detection F1 > 0.90 on keystone set; critical hallucinations < 2%
- Reliability: no more than 1% errors/timeouts during business hours
- Cost: we’ll use the trial run to validate TCO - target is < $X per 1M tokens (we'll provide a target once procurement weighs in)

We can kick off the technical call on Thu Jun 25 10:00 PT - that works for Tom and me. Please send calendar invite and sample replay format.

Elaine
Director, Product — Recommendations
SaaSify
elaine.park@saasify.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@saasify.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T13:18:00Z
Subject: Re: POC Trial Planning — Recap & workload intake

Perfect — thanks for the numbers, Elaine. That gives us a clear starting point. A few notes and the next items from Redwood:

1) Initial capacity recommendation (trial):
- We’ll provision a hosted trial cluster tuned for mid-high throughput: capacity to sustain 120 RPS with headroom for 240 RPS 3-min bursts.
- We’ll enable prefix caching and aggressive batching for recommendation flows; Marissa will tune batch sizes based on the sample replay.

2) Evaluation plan & observability:
- Redwood will provide per-route dashboards (latency p50/p95/p99, error rates), token-level cost breakdown, and request tracing for a set of keystone prompts.
- We’ll run the keystone quality suite daily and share results in a single dashboard.

3) Timeline / owners:
- Thu Jun 25: Kickoff (10:00 PT) - access + sample replay format (Owner: Ben / Marissa).
- Fri Jun 26: Sample replay ingest & first smoke run (Owner: Marissa / Dylan).
- Week 1 (Jun 29-Jul 3): Replay-driven tuning & run day-long soak.
- Week 2 (Jul 6-10): Focused keystone quality checks and A/B prompt variants.
- Week 3 (Jul 13-17): Final validation and procurement sync.

4) Action items for SaaSify before kickoff:
- Upload 48-hour anonymized sample replay to the Drive folder.
- Share a service account or API key with read-only permissions for the replay files.
- Confirm any restricted data handling requirements (PII redaction, retention windows).

If that timeline works we’ll lock the kickoff invite and Marissa will share the replay ingestion template.

—
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@saasify.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: POC Trial Planning — Replay format & quick QA note

Hi Elaine / Ben — quick technical note ahead of the kickoff.

Thanks for the profile — the numbers look reasonable. For the sample replay please include:
- CSV or NDJSON with fields: request_id, timestamp, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, route, user_id_hash (anonymized), any attachments referenced (filenames only).
- Include a small set (~200-500) of keystone prompts in a separate file for the daily quality suite.
- If you have traces that show end-to-end latency (client → Redwood), include those as well - they help isolate client-side vs. model latency.

A few things I’ll check during the smoke run:
- That batching behaves as expected for 75 token prompts / 210 token completions.
- That the 9% long-context requests (>1024 tokens) don't cause memory pressure - if they do we’ll test a quantization profile and/or route them to a larger context instance.

I’ll send the replay ingestion template and a short checklist after this - see you on Thu 10:00 PT.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
